display.title: The Alter Rebbe Frees the Chassan, Part 1
display.summary_short: Why Hillel taught Ahavas Yisroel as 'don't do', and how a cruel police chief seized an orphan chassan on his wedding day, until the Alter Rebbe arrived.
display.summary_long: Coming from Yud Shevat in the week of Tu B'Shvat, the storyteller asks a class of children a question about Ahavas Yisroel, the first of the Rebbe's mitzvah campaigns: why did Hillel tell the convert what not to do, instead of what to do? He gives the Tzemach Tzedek's answer: we overlook our own faults because we love ourselves, so we should overlook other people's faults too and see only their good. Then the story begins. In a town near Liozna, two orphans raised by kind families are engaged, and the Alter Rebbe himself helped make the shidduch. The whole town helps with the wedding except the richest man, who only ever gives one rusty coin. On the wedding day the Jew-hating police chief seizes the chassan for the Czar's army and threatens to send anyone who pleads for him to Siberia. At noon the Alter Rebbe arrives and sets out for the police station with the town's Rav. Before continuing, the storyteller shares the Maharal's custom for Shabbos Shirah of letting children feed the birds. To be continued.
display.lesson: Love every Jew the way you love yourself: overlook their faults just as you overlook your own, and look only at their good.
